in_hebrew.name: ריקארדו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ריקארדו הוא שם שמקורו בגרמנית ומשמעותו 'עשיר בכוח רוחני' או 'מנהיג חזק'. השם נגזר מהמילים 'ריך' שמשמעותו 'עשיר' ו'הארד' שמשמעותו 'כוח' או 'חוזק'. השם ריקארדו לא מופיע ישירות במקרא, אך הוא קשור למושגים של עושר רוחני וכוח פנימי, שעליהם מדגישים כתבי הקודש.

in_greek.name: Ρικάρδο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ρικάρδο προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'πλούσιος σε πνευματική δύναμη' ή 'ισχυρός ηγέτης'. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος συνδέεται με τις λέξεις 'reich' που σημαίνει 'πλούσιος' και 'hard' που σημαίνει 'δύναμη' ή 'ισχύς'. Αν και το όνομα Ρικάρδο δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα στη Νέα Διαθήκη, εκφράζει έννοιες πνευματικής πλούτου και εσωτερικής δύναμης, που είναι κεντρικές στη χριστιανική διδασκαλία.

in_latin.name: Riccardo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Riccardo origine germanico derivatur et significat 'dives in virtute' seu 'potens dux'. Etymologia nominis coniungitur cum vocibus 'reich' quod significat 'dives' et 'hard' quod significat 'virtus' seu 'potentia'. Quamquam nomen Riccardo non directe in Scripturis apparet, tamen conceptos exprimit divitiarum spiritualium et roboris interioris, quae in doctrina christiana eminentur.

in_english.name: Riccardo
in_english.meaning: Rich in spiritual power, powerful leader
in_english.long_meaning: The name Riccardo, of Germanic origin, means 'rich in spiritual power' or 'powerful leader'. It is derived from the words 'reich' meaning 'rich' and 'hard' meaning 'power' or 'strength'. Although Riccardo is not directly mentioned in the Bible, it conveys concepts of spiritual wealth and inner strength, which are central to Christian teachings. Historically, the name has been associated with leadership and spiritual richness, reflecting the values of courage, faith, and determination.

The underlying meaning of 'rich in power, ruling with strength' echoes the divine attributes of God – Omnipotent, All-powerful, and All-knowing. historical_references.reference: Riccardo IV, Duke of York (1411-1460) was a key figure in the Wars of the Roses during the late Middle Ages. He was the eldest son of Richard, 3rd Duke of York, and Cecily Neville. Known as 'the Red Rose of York', he was a prominent leader of the House of York in the struggle for the English throne against the House of Lancaster, represented by the White Rose of Lancaster. He was killed at the Battle of Wakefield in 1460.
historical_references.context: English civil war between the Houses of York and Lancaster for the throne

historical_references.reference: Riccardo da Sebeto (c. 1243-1325) was a Cistercian monk and theologian, best known for his criticism of Thomas Aquinas' philosophical theology. He was born in Sebeto, near Florence, Italy, and studied theology in Paris. His main work is 'De Errore Theologicis Noviter Consurgentibus', where he criticized Aquinas' synthesis of Aristotelian philosophy and Christian theology, arguing for a more radical adherence to the Bible and the Fathers of the Church.
historical_references.context: Philosophical debates within the Christian theological tradition
